title: QUIC Compatible Version Negotiation (RFC 9368)
purpose: Capture the RFC 9368 version_information transport-parameter floor and the compatible-version runtime behavior that the repository now implements.
scope: This specification covers the RFC 9368 version_information transport-parameter floor and compatible-version runtime behavior: endpoints format and parse authenticated Version Information, the server selects a mutually supported compatible version from the client's offered set, the client adopts and validates the negotiated version, and the authenticated chosen-version checks keep the connection version consistent. It does not cover Retry or 0-RTT compatibility follow-ons beyond the RFC 9368 compatibility and security rules already written here.
context: RFC 9368 defines authenticated Version Information for QUIC and uses it to prevent downgrade attacks while allowing compatible version negotiation. The repository now carries the transport-parameter, bridge-state, listener-bootstrap, and runtime version-switch plumbing for both the floor and the compatible-version runtime-selection slice.

requirements.title: Emit authenticated Version Information
requirements.statement: An endpoint that supports compatible version negotiation MUST encode Version Information in the `version_information` transport parameter with a non-zero Chosen Version and a list of Available Versions that includes the Chosen Version when the endpoint acts as a client.

requirements.title: Parse peer Version Information
requirements.statement: Both endpoints MUST parse their peer's Version Information during the handshake.

requirements.title: Close on Version Information parsing failure
requirements.statement: If parsing Version Information fails, such as when it is too short or its length is not divisible by four, the endpoint MUST close the connection.

requirements.title: Reject zero Version Information values
requirements.statement: If an endpoint receives a Chosen Version equal to zero, or any Available Version equal to zero, it MUST treat it as a parsing failure.

requirements.title: Reject missing client Chosen Version preference
requirements.statement: If a server receives Version Information where the Chosen Version is not included in Available Versions, it MUST treat it as a parsing failure.

requirements.title: Select a compatible negotiated version
requirements.statement: When an endpoint can parse the client's first flight using the client's Chosen Version and the client's Version Information lists at least one mutually supported compatible version, the server MUST select one such version as the Negotiated Version, continue the handshake using that version, and preserve the client's Original Version long enough to authenticate the Version Information carried on that original first flight.

requirements.title: Adopt and validate the negotiated version
requirements.statement: A client that learns the Negotiated Version from the server's handshake packets MUST validate that the server's Chosen Version matches the Negotiated Version and close the connection with a version negotiation error if they do not match. When the negotiated version is compatible with the client's Original Version, the client continues the connection using that negotiated version for subsequent packets.

supplemental_sections.heading: RFC 9368 Section 4.3 Split Mapping
supplemental_sections.content: The retired local requirement REQ-QUIC-RFC9368-S3-0002 mixed several parser-failure obligations. It has been split across RFC9368-S4-P3-S1-R01, RFC9368-S4-P3-S2-R01, RFC9368-S4-P3-S3-R01, and RFC9368-S4-P3-S4-R01. RFC9368-S4-P3-S2-R01 remains an explicit gap because current tests only prove malformed Version Information is detected as a parser failure at the transport-parameter codec boundary; they do not prove endpoint connection-close behavior.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This slice owns the authenticated Version Information floor and the compatible-version runtime-selection flow. It keeps the original-version authentication path alive long enough to validate the client's Version Information, then switches the server and client runtime state to the negotiated version when compatible negotiation succeeds. Retry and 0-RTT compatibility follow-ons remain separate future work.
